Go ahead.
How many people would we be running payroll for? And have you ever outsourced it before?
Forty-two, growing to sixty. And yes — it went badly, which is why we’re here.
That helps. Our fee structure depends on headcount, not on hours, so at sixty it is predictable.
And what exactly would we get every month?

Have you done this for a foreign parent company before?

Hi, it's David. I've been through your proposal twice now, so thank you for turning it around quickly. Two things. The scope looks right, and the fee structure actually makes sense to me, which is more than I can say for the other two. But the onboarding worries me. You've put six weeks from signature, and we open in four. I need to know whether that is a hard number or whether there is a way around it. The other thing is that head office hasn't approved the budget yet, so I can't sign anything this week even if I want to. Call me back when you can.

You asked why we've stayed with them for seven years. Honestly? Because nothing happens. We signed with them the month we opened the Brazilian entity, and in seven years they have never missed a payroll deadline. Not once. Our first provider missed two in the first quarter, and I spent that whole year apologising to people about their own salaries. And compliance, which used to keep me awake, I haven't thought about since they took over. That is what I'm paying for. Not the reports. The silence.
